fieldMarks: Male: glossy black with a contrasting brown head
Female: plain dusty brown with a dark, sparrowlike bill
behavior: Forages mostly walking on the ground, often with cattle or horses catching flushed insects; originally associated with bison herds
Seeds are about half of the summer diet and over 90% in winter; the rest mostly insects
Migrants may begin leaving nesting areas by July or August; present all year in many southern areas
Squeaky gurgle; call is a check or rattle
habitat: Open or semi-open country year-round: farms, fields, prairies, wood edges and river groves; in winter concentrates in farmland, pastures and feedlots.
range: Breeds from southeast Alaska, northern British Columbia and southern Mackenzie to Newfoundland, south to central Mexico, the Gulf Coast and southern Florida; winters from the northern U.S. south.
